appraisal_events.evidence: il avait aperçu à quelque distance de sa Rachel la Rachel petite poule, la Rachel réelle, à supposer que la Rachel poule fût plus réelle que l'autre... une Rachel à vingt francs
appraisal_events.explanation: Recognized by two cheap 'poules' at the station, Rachel briefly appears to Saint-Loup as a devalued double of the woman he has idealized, imagined as an ordinary 'grue' worth twenty francs rather than the composed figure he loves; the vision is heavily hedged with 'peut-être' and 'à supposer que', so it is reported as a tentative perception rather than a settled fact.

appraisal_events.evidence: sa liaison avec Rachel, au contraire, était ce qui l'avait mis un peu hors du monde, faisait qu'il y était moins coté
appraisal_events.explanation: The narrator states directly that Saint-Loup's liaison with Rachel has lowered his standing, placing him partly outside fashionable society, in contrast to the easy social credit his name and looks would otherwise bring him.

status_effects.explanation: Rachel's worth is momentarily called into question when Saint-Loup glimpses her as interchangeable with common 'poules', though this reading is tentative and quickly recedes.
Saint-Loup's local social standing is diminished because his costly liaison with Rachel is explicitly said to have placed him partly outside the world he would otherwise move freely in.

ambiguities: The vision of a cheaper 'Rachel à vingt francs' is presented as Robert's subjective and heavily hedged perception ('peut-être', 'à supposer que'), not a stable narrator-endorsed fact, so it materially weakens how firmly Rachel's diminishment should be read.
